Check a study's SPEC against the packages installed: one call

Source: R/check_spec.R
tfl_check_spec.Rd

Everything tflspec can say about a study's reports before their programs run, in one table, each row at one of three levels – the person's definition of 2026-10-29:

Usage

tfl_check_spec(study, output_id = NULL, build = FALSE)

Arguments

study

A study read with tfl_read_study_spec(), or its folder.

output_id

The reports to check; NULL for every report.

build

TRUE: each report the checks above pass is also built (tfl_check_build()) – its data read, its ARD made, its table, listing or figure object made, no RTF – so that a report with no row can be made; one that cannot has an error row, part "build". A few seconds a report. FALSE (default): the checks above only.

Value

A data frame, one row a problem: output_id (NA for the study's ARD definition as a whole), part ("file", "ard", "content", "program", "figure", "build"), item (the file, the analysis, the function and argument, or the figure's part and field), level ("error", "warning", "note", "check") and message. Its attributes: versions, a data frame of the key packages (package, installed, NA when not installed); ids, the reports checked (the OK ones too); kinds, each report's kind, named by id; outputs_dir, the folder the report files are in, from the study folder.

Details

  • error: the file cannot be read as a SPEC (its YAML, or a key or a value the schema does not have, an analysis the ARD definition refuses): the report cannot be copied into the study;

  • warning: the SPEC reads, but a program that runs cannot be written from it (the ARD program or the table's code stops; a content function the installed rtfreporter does not have yet);

  • note: the program is written all the same – an argument the installed cards / cardx does not know, a version to look at.

A report with no error and no warning row is OK: its code is written (whether the report is right is another matter). What the AI marked to confirm (ai: confirm, tfl_ai_confirm()) is a row of level check, apart from the three: it does not keep a report from being adopted. tfl_check_reports() gives the three levels a report at a time, with its confirms; tfl_check_fix_text() writes, for a report at error or warning, the text to paste into the agent's chat.

Each report is read and checked on its own: a file that cannot be read is an error of that report (by its file's name) and stops no other. The checks: each report's ARD definition against the installed cards / cardx (tfl_ard_spec(), written as its program, tfl_ard_code()), its content items against the schema and the installed rtfreporter (tfl_schema_check(), the items of an appended part too; its code written, tfl_content_code()), and a figure's design against the installed ggplot2 and the version it is written for (tfl_check_fig_design()). The packages' installed versions come with it, as an attribute. A GUI's check button and the AI's run call it.

See also

tfl_check_reports(), tfl_check_fix_text(), tfl_ard_spec(), tfl_schema_check(), tfl_check_fig_design()

Examples

if (requireNamespace("haven", quietly = TRUE)) {
  # a study of the bundled ADSL, with one report
  d <- file.path(tempfile(), "study")
  dir.create(file.path(d, "adam"), recursive = TRUE)
  chr <- function(x) if (is.factor(x)) as.character(x) else x
  haven::write_xpt(as.data.frame(lapply(adsl, chr)), file.path(d, "adam", "adsl.xpt"))
  tfl_ai_study_init(d, adam = "adam", study_id = "EX-1")
  tfl_write_output(
    tfl_output("T-DM", "table", population = "SAF",
               template = list(name = "demog", args = list(population = "SAF"))),
    file.path(d, "spec", "outputs", "T-DM.yml"))
  p <- tfl_check_spec(d)
  p
  tfl_check_reports(p)
  attr(p, "versions")
}
#>       package   installed
#> 1     tflspec 0.0.24.9238
#> 2 rtfreporter  0.8.2.9100
#> 3       cards       0.9.0
#> 4       cardx       0.3.4
#> 5     ggplot2       4.0.3
